title: TransMem — where the paper and the code part ways
subtitle: Only the divergent steps are drawn, all sitting inside the single forward-pass mechanism (B6/B7) since that's the only place this system's write+read logic lives.
source: paper arXiv:2607.29032v1  x  repo TransMem @ 6d7a612   ·   servers/transmem/verification.md, 121 assertions checked (92 correct / 2 wrong / 25 partial / 2 unverifiable)
footer: memory-bench · methodology flow · paper ↔ code divergence
legend_notes: Prefill is not intervention-free. Paper Eq.1's prose ("TransMem does not intervene in generation" during prefill, txt:175-177) is contradicted by the code's own control flow: the forward hook is registered at layered.py:519-520 before the single prefill call at :528, and that call's prefill branch (:487-499) both reads H_M and writes the correction (:512) in the same pass. code-architecture.md repeats the wrong claim and even cites the wrong line number (:565).

Gate granularity is the one architecture-level mismatch neither source document caught: paper Eq.6-7 specify a per-dimension vector gate (W_g in R^(dxd), elementwise product); the code hard-locks gate_granularity to "token_scalar" (nn.Linear(dim,1)) — an order-of-magnitude parameter-count difference. Ironically the paper's own appendix (txt:1344-1347) already describes scalar-gate behavior; it's the paper's main text that is the outlier.

Three more mechanical parameters silently drift: memory-slot count (paper's stated optimum B=5 vs. code's B=4 everywhere), the segment-end position formula (paper's literal h_L vs. code's default floor-mode approximation), and the correction start position (paper's Eq.7 t>=L+1 vs. code's len_cq-1).

Chunk-wise overflow, presented in the paper as part of the method (txt:328-345), is entirely a caller-side, default-off feature in the code, and the benchmark's own LoCoMo eval script never triggers it at all — this answers a question the paper-architecture.md review had flagged as open (P50).
